children.label: Structure and classification
children: Aromatic ring (lipophilic), intermediate chain, tertiary amine (hydrophilic)
Esters: cocaine, procaine, chloroprocaine
Amides (two i's): lidocaine, prilocaine, bupivacaine, etidocaine, mepivacaine
Esters: unstable, hydrolyzed by plasma cholinesterase, PABA allergy
Amides: stable, slowly metabolized by liver, longer acting, allergy extremely rare

children.label: Mechanism
children: Block Na+ channels, inhibiting the action potential in unmyelinated fibres
Only the unionized base crosses the membrane
Acidic tissue (abscess, inflammation): less free base, weak or failed block
Adding sodium bicarbonate raises pH and gives more base

children.label: Preparations
children: Acidic solutions (pH 4-5.5), hydrochloride salts
May contain vasoconstrictor, reducing agent (metabisulphite), preservative
1% = 10 mg/mL (mg/mL = % x 10)

children.label: Vasoconstrictors
children: Adrenaline 1:80,000 to 1:300,000 is most common
Slow absorption, lower toxicity, longer duration, less bleeding
Maximum dose: lidocaine 3 mg/kg plain, 7 with adrenaline
Maximum dose: prilocaine 6 plain, 9 with adrenaline; bupivacaine 2 either way
Never use around end-arteries (fingers, penis) or in IVRA
Relative: severe hypertension, GA with halothane

children.label: Clinical uses
children: Topical: lidocaine gel, EMLA (lidocaine 2.5% + prilocaine 2.5%)
Infiltration for minor surgery
Peripheral nerve blocks (nerve stimulator or ultrasound)
Intravenous regional anesthesia, spinal, epidural
Always aspirate before injecting

children.label: IVRA (Bier's block)
children: Upper limb surgery under 1 h
Two cannulae: one in the affected limb, one in the other limb for resuscitation
Exsanguinate with Esmarch band, inflate proximal cuff above systolic pressure
Inject lidocaine or prilocaine after removing the band
Cuff stays inflated at least 20 min, then deflate gradually
Never bupivacaine or etidocaine: cardiotoxic

children.label: Individual agents
children: Lidocaine: first amide, local anesthetic and antiarrhythmic, blocks fast Na+ channels
Bupivacaine: long duration, most cardiotoxic, not given IV, used spinal or epidural
Benzocaine: topical only, causes methemoglobinemia

children.label: Toxicity
children: Causes: accidental IV injection, rapid absorption from vascular sites, overdose
CNS first: dizziness, tinnitus, circumoral numbness, blurred vision, metallic taste
Severe: convulsions, coma, respiratory arrest
CVS: bradycardia and hypotension without adrenaline; myocardial depression leads to collapse
Prevent: secure IV access and have resuscitation equipment ready
Treat: stop injection, call help, ABC, O2, ventilate, fluids, ephedrine, atropine
Convulsions: diazepam 0.2-0.4 mg/kg or thiopentone 1-4 mg/kg

children.label: Antidotes
children: Bupivacaine: 20% lipid emulsion IV (Intralipid, not a true antidote)
Benzocaine methemoglobinemia: low-dose methylene blue
Lidocaine: diphenhydramine (as written on the slide)
